newsitem.title: UK: Minor Metals - Scant interest during Metals Week.
newsitem.headline: Minor Metals - Scant interest during Metals Week.

text.p: Minor metals trading was largely subdued during the past week and prices generally showed little movement.
But traders said this was not surprising when many traders and their customers were at the London annual Metals Week.
Antimony remained under downside pressure, while cobalt was showing signs of easing as an influential player targeted lower price for both high grade and Russian material.
Offers of Chinese metal and a lack of real buying interest in anticipation of further price retracements saw the antimony market dip lower.
Several European traders believed that antimony had the potential to decline further, but reiterated concerns that in the long-term such a move could dent both producers and consumers.

They suggested the recent Chinese offer was an attempt to generate cash flow, adding most business is normally in dollars. Downside targets were pegged at $2,000 a tonne. The recent robust performance of cobalt looked to be finding upside resistance in most areas of the market as one player expected lower prices near-term against the backdrop of undivided opinions of market fundamentals.

"There has been selling at recent stable levels after the market stalled," one trader said. This side of the market were looking for high grade and Russian material below $20 a l/b near-term. One trader said the recent of upside progress has left several market operators wary to further falls after the rally from 23-month lows of $18/$19 in August, basis Russian metal.

"The market looked destined for $30 following the spike from the lows, though this found little follow-through interest which prompted the liquidation," one trader commented. He believed new-stream production towards the end of the 1990s could play a role in upsetting the relatively balanced supply/demand situation that currently prevails.
But others argued that demand will outstrip supply, given the growing demand from the battery and super-alloy industries.

"The are long-term forward contracts currently in play from the alloy industry, while currently a scarp tightness reamins, " one upside trader said. But he noted near-term there was little interest from consumers.
Other metals remained quiet at little changed levels.

Magnesium in all its myriad forms was basically steady, though several traders were expecting price movements next week as traders and customers returned to their desks following Metals Week. Molybdenum held stable as traders continued to digest recent concentrate shortages and a lack of offers from China.
